requirements.requirement: Treat /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the authoritative source of truth
requirements.summary: app.conf was created on node1 (root-owned, 644) as the canonical file, and all subsequent edits used as the propagation trigger were made exclusively on node1; node2's copy was always derived from node1 via pull, never edited directly.

requirements.requirement: Keep node2's copy of app.conf synchronized with node1, picking up changes within 15 minutes
requirements.summary: A cron job on node2 pulls app.conf from node1 over passwordless SSH every 5 minutes (well inside the 15-minute bound) and applies it only on checksum change. The crontab entry was directly observed installed and active.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate that a real change on node1 automatically propagates to node2 without manual intervention
requirements.summary: Two independent end-to-end tests directly observed automatic propagation: (1) node1 was edited to sha256 ca64030e...; the node2 sync log recorded an unattended cron-triggered sync at :40:01 and node2's file checksum matched node1's exactly. (2) After both nodes were rebooted, node1 was edited again (sha256 6c9387db...) and the node2 sync log recorded another unattended cron-triggered sync at :55:01 with matching checksum, confirming the mechanism is durable, not a one-off manual run.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (independent of task contract) covering both managed nodes
requirements.summary: For both node1 and node2: pre-restart boot_id and healthy service/data state were captured, shutdown -r now was acknowledged, connection timeouts were observed during the down window, a new boot_id was captured on reconnect (node1: 33b0e84c...->2c436ff6...; node2: 95e2f83d...->1f00229c...), and post-restart recovery of sshd/crond, the cron entry, and file content/checksum was directly confirmed on both nodes. This is cross-checked by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare vs after_executor), which independently confirm the boot_id change on both nodes.

overall_summary: The executor established node1's app.conf as the source of truth, deployed a cron-driven pull-based sync on node2 running every 5 minutes (within the 15-minute requirement), and directly verified two independent unattended propagation events (one before and one after a full reboot of both nodes), with checksums matching in each case. The provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated on both nodes with pre/post boot-identity, service, and data evidence, cross-checked against the fixed global snapshots. The only notable issue is a small, low-risk temp-file residue left by an abandoned background wait-job experiment on node2 that was not cleaned up.
limitations: Clock skew is visible in the raw timestamps (node2 showing 'Aug 26' dates against the executor's 'Sep 29' session), but the sync log's internal timestamps consistently align to 5-minute cron boundaries (:40:01, :55:01) both before and after reboot, which supports genuine unattended cron execution rather than manual triggering.

Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (timed out) in both the before_prepare and after_executor global snapshots on both nodes, so package-state integrity could not be independently confirmed beyond the executor's own command trace.

Long-term durability beyond the observed test window (two independent 5-minute sync cycles, including one post-reboot) was not directly observed over a longer horizon, though the evidence gives reasonable confidence in ongoing operation.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were purposeful (SSH keypair install, app.conf creation, sync script, crontab entry, restart cycle) and either persisted as intended or were bounded byproducts of a legitimate restart. One mutation had no lasting causal role: cmd-521c2521e51948fa launched a detached nohup background job on node2 (sleep 320; date >> /tmp/waitmark.log) intended to gate a later wait, but the subsequent wait-for-it command (cmd-99f7f0a394f34b0c) failed on a proxy timeout and was abandoned in favor of simple sleep N polling instead (cmd-0a627e4cd2d54877, cmd-56b50b25a81e4970). This orphaned background-job attempt left temp residue (/tmp/wait.out, /tmp/wait.pid) visible in the after_executor snapshot on node2 that was never cleaned up. The residue is low-risk (temp files only, self-terminating background process, no service or security impact) but was not reverted. The /tmp/reboot.out files left on both nodes are a minor, low-risk byproduct of the legitimate, task-relevant restart action rather than an unnecessary mutation.
